before: always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n_enter) begin
after: always_ff @(posedge clk or posedge rst_n_enter) begin
proposal.description: The second stage's asynchronous event is the rising edge of rst_n_enter instead of the falling edge, so rst_n_exit no longer asserts the instant rst_n_enter falls - it waits for the next clk edge.
proposal.reason: When rst_n_enter falls between clock edges (or while clk is stopped) rst_n_exit stays high until the next posedge clk, instead of going low with zero clock latency; a low pulse that fits between two clock edges never reaches rst_n_exit at all.

before: always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n_enter) begin
proposal.description: The first stage clears synchronously only: meta_ff is not put back to 0 by a reset assertion that does not span a clk edge, so it keeps its 1 from before the reset.
proposal.reason: After a rst_n_enter low pulse shorter than a clock period (or any assertion with no clk edge inside it), rst_n_exit is cleared but meta_ff is still 1, so rst_n_exit releases on the first clock after release instead of the second - the two-clock synchronous release is lost.

why: make lint already catches it: make lint: SYNCASYNCNET
